chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Maktab told us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) cursed the wasila and the mustawsila, meaning the female fornicator and the female procurer.

key_terms.الوَاصِلَة: The female fornicator; one who engages in illicit sexual intercourse.
key_terms.الْقَوَّادَة: The female procurer; one who leads or guides others to fornication.
key_terms.وَالْمُسْتَوْصِلَة: The female procurer or matchmaker who facilitates the fornication.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of wasila and mustawsila in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific linguistic usage of 'al-wasila' and 'al-mustawsila' as referring to the female fornicator and the female procurer, respectively, linking them to the divine curse reported from the Prophet. This interpretation highlights the semantic flexibility of these terms in early Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing them from their more common theological meaning of 'intercession' or 'means of approach' to God. The hadith underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition in defining social roles and their spiritual consequences within the Shia scholarly tradition.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Hussain bin Ibrahim bin Ahmad bin Hisham al-Maktab, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Ibrahim bin Ziyad al-Karkhi, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, cursed the wasila and the mustawsila, meaning the female fornicator and the female procurer.
